txt: Much higher odds of heavy rain and flooding as warm water and convection shift east. Strongest in Eastern-Pacific events.
Suppressed convection brings drought, heat, and elevated fire/haze risk.
Reduced winter-spring rainfall, delayed monsoon, heightened bushfire risk.
Negative rainfall and positive temperature anomalies; severe risk to rain-fed agriculture.
Wetter 'short rains', especially when reinforced by a positive Indian Ocean Dipole.
On average wetter, cooler, stormier winter as the Pacific jet strengthens and shifts south.
Tends toward milder, drier conditions than normal.
Drought and elevated fire risk; can flip the tropical biosphere to a net carbon source.
Tendency toward a weaker/delayed summer monsoon, though the relationship is non-stationary.
Increased odds of higher mean and extreme rainfall.
Hurricane activity is generally suppressed by increased vertical wind shear (exceptions occur).
Tropical cyclone activity tends to increase relative to the Atlantic.
